title: Dynamic AMF topology, cytoplasmic flow and trade-network co-evolution

source.source_scope: in-vitro 2D-constrained AMF network growth and ROI-linked flow observations

biological_scope.host: Daucus carota in-vitro root organ culture
biological_scope.geometry: split Petri plate, root compartment and fungus-only compartment

evaluation_tracks.name: network_efficiency_and_construction_cost
evaluation_tracks.note: Reproduce the exact article normalization and reference-graph construction; do not substitute unnormalized shortest-path efficiency.

evaluation_tracks.name: temporal_generalization
evaluation_tracks.holdout_policy: fit early time windows, predict later time windows; never randomize adjacent frames across train and test

model_families.description: Source-provided graph and measured flow, used as reference where available
Topology-based efficiency with no measured-flow model
Constant edge geometry and flow baseline
Interpolate observed flow from training ROIs / edges only
Predict flow from qualified edge geometry and measured training data
Dynamic graph, edge geometry, measured-flow observations and resource/cost constraints

forbidden_splits: random edge split across same replicate
ROI leakage from validation to training
split_contract.reporting: pooled, per-strain, per-replicate and worst-stratum results

scientific_hypotheses_to_test: tip-density pulse leads the trailing hyphal filament-density wave
trailing filament density approaches a strain-specific saturation profile
fusion/anastomosis contributes to network density regulation
normalized root-directed efficiency remains approximately stable while normalized global efficiency rises
edge radius is associated with betweenness centrality
measured flow speeds and/or fluxes vary with network position and edge geometry
bidirectional and antiparallel flow coexist in the same network
early tipward/rootward velocity asymmetry weakens with network age
claim_boundaries: graph shortest-path efficiency is not measured cytoplasmic flow
flow velocity is not volumetric flow without cross-sectional area and geometry
volumetric flow is not nutrient delivery without concentration and transport terms
tracer enrichment is not automatically direct fungal transport
the in-vitro 2D plate is not a 3D soil network
findings from the three AMF profiles do not establish a universal rule for septate fungi, endophytes or saprotrophs

proposed_targets_not_results.exact_reproduction: reproduce available main-figure source tables within published uncertainty and documented numerical tolerance
proposed_targets_not_results.uncertainty: nominal 90% and 95% interval coverage evaluated by strain and time horizon
proposed_targets_not_results.graph_flow_model: outperform topology-only, uniform-flow and shuffled-flow controls on preregistered held-out flow prediction tasks
proposed_targets_not_results.generalization: leave-one-strain-out and complete-replicate holdouts before a cross-strain claim
proposed_targets_not_results.cost_efficiency: plot prediction error and calibration against runtime, memory and data-processing cost

receipt_requirements: Figshare article version and complete file inventory
image/graph/flow processing configuration and observation cadence
replicate, strain and ROI identity mapping
MST/DT reference graph construction and normalization method
per-track metrics, held-out results and worst-stratum results
